findings.title: Includes a Linux kernel header
findings.message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP is not believed to ship them (guess; not checked against an SDP). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can often be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.
findings.remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface instead.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: ls $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/linux and asm* before treating these as missing.

findings.title: CPU affinity (sched_setaffinity & friends)
findings.message: Linux affinity API.
findings.remedy: Use ThreadCtl(_NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK, &mask) for the calling thread (recalled QNX API; needs privilege). The mask is a bit set of CPU indices. Semantics are narrower: Linux sched_setaffinity(pid, ...) can target another process or thread, the runmask call applies to the calling thread, so per-pid callers need restructuring.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: ThreadCtl runmask argument layout.

findings.title: sendfile/splice zero-copy calls
findings.message: Linux zero-copy file transfer calls. sendfile() also exists on BSDs with a different signature, so a same-named call may compile but misbehave.
findings.remedy: Fall back to a read()/write() loop (or mmap + write) behind a small helper; add a platform fast path only if profiling demands it.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: some of these may exist with other semantics.

findings.title: Linux-specific socket options
findings.message: Socket options that originated on Linux. Some exist on BSD-derived stacks with a different meaning or struct layout (TCP_FASTOPEN and TCP_INFO exist on FreeBSD; TCP_INFO's struct differs). QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present, so presence on 8.0 must be checked per option (guess). Not all of these are Linux-only.
findings.remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. If the macro IS defined, confirm the semantics and struct layout before relying on a same-named constant (TCP_INFO in particular).
findings.verify: verify against SDP: grep each option in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/netinet/tcp.h and sys/socket.h.

findings.title: Autotools project with no QNX host support
findings.message: No QNX mention in the tree. Old bundled config.sub/config.guess may not recognise a QNX host triplet.
findings.remedy: Refresh config.sub/config.guess (autoreconf -fi or copy from a current automake), then configure with --host=<cpu>-unknown-nto-qnx<version> and CC set to qcc.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: exact host triplet format for 8.0.
